subject: Workplace Skills
title: Exercise as a Productivity Tool
description: One-minute skill: Exercise as a Productivity Tool.

hook.text: A 20-minute walk boosts creative thinking by 60%, according to Stanford research on divergent thought.

buildup.text: Exercise increases blood flow to the brain, releases BDNF, and improves working memory for hours after.

discovery.text: BDNF is brain-derived neurotrophic factor. It grows new neural connections. Exercise is brain fertilizer.

twist.text: You don't need a gym. Even light movement like a walk or stretching session delivers cognitive benefits.

climax.text: Schedule movement before your hardest work block. The post-exercise cognitive boost peaks at 60 minutes.

punchline.text: Move your body. Your brain will thank you.

quiz.question: What is BDNF and why does exercise matter for the brain?
options: A hormone that reduces stress but not cognitive function
A protein that grows new neural connections, boosted by exercise
A neurotransmitter that only improves mood
